answer: Topology Harbor Rule. Each agent must maintain at least two persistent, latency-verified routes to distinct incumbents; routes form a karst of sparse, irregular links observable network-wide. New agents can only harbor at the network edge until they sustain three independent, non-clustered contacts over time. Sybils created in bulk connect cheaply to each other but cannot bridge the canyon between their cluster and the incumbent core without paying real latency and relay costs per identity, scaling linearly with each fake node.
